claims.claim: Scene, the Commemoratio: 'praefati nuntii XVII Kal Augusti adierunt ecclesiam Sanctae Sophiae et super obstinatione illius conquesti clero ex more ad missas praeparato jam hora tertia diei sabbati chartam excommunicationis super principale altare posuerunt sub oculis praesentis cleri et populi. Inde mox egressi etiam pulverem pedum suorum excussere in testimonium illis juxta dictum evangelii proclamantes: Videat Deus et judicet'. Will reads XVII Kal. Aug. as 16 July (his note 80 to the Edict). The brief gives 'a Saturday in July' and names both readings (Will 16 July; Mirbt 13 July)
claims.witness: WILL (will_acta-et-scripta-de-controversiis-ecclesiae-graecae-et-latinae-saec-xi-grc-lat_1861.txt) l.14825-14827, 14872-14880; Will's note l.16294-16295 [two-column OCR interleaved; OCR forms 'Sic?ab', 'juxta*']

claims.claim: Envoys named: 'advenientibus a domino papa Leone nono apocrisiariis sanctae Romanae et Apostolicae sedis, Humberto scilicet cardinali episcopo Silvae Candidae et Petro Amalphitanorum archiepiscopo, Friderico quoque diacono et cancellario', the day 'ipso die nativitatis beati Ioannis Baptistae' (24 June) belongs to Nicetas's recantation ('anathematizavit'), with the envoys' coming as background, 'Anno duodecimo imperii Constantini Monomachi indictione VII'
claims.witness: WILL (will_acta-et-scripta-de-controversiis-ecclesiae-graecae-et-latinae-saec-xi-grc-lat_1861.txt) l.14779-14783, 14803-14804; MIRBT (mirbt_quellen-zur-geschichte-des-papsttums-3e-aufl-deu-lat_1911.txt) l.9876-9879 [OCR 'scilicet' split as 'sci- licet' across columns; Mirbt OCR 'eardinali']

claims.claim: Will on authorship of the Commemoratio: 'Quum igitur Humbertus, ut ex multis indiciis apparet, legationis princeps fuerit, dubitari vix potest, quin hoc quoque scriptum ... ab eodem profectum sit'; Sigebert and Ekkehard: 'Humbertus episcopus Silvae candidae haec descripsit, et scripta Nicetae monachi et Leonis Achridani Bulgarum archiepiscopi confutavit'

Leo of Ohrid's letter of 1053, at Keroularios's urging: 'Quo tempore (1053) instigante Michaéle Caerulario ... Leo, archiepiscopus Achridanus, incendium discordiae inopinato suscitavit epistola ad Ioannem, episcopum Tranensem'; the date is Will's

Humbert wrote the Dialogue at Constantinople: Will, 'Humbertus, princeps legatorum, per scripta cum eo agere cogeretur. Is tum Dialogum inter Romanum et Graecum ... composuit'; Wibert of Toul's Life of Leo IX, quoted by Will: 'Praedictus etiam frater Humbertus edidit contra eorum putida scripta responsionem instar dialogi, ab ipso Latine scriptam apocrisariatus sui tempore Constantinopoli, et jussu imperatoris ... Constantini Monomachi Graece editam, sub nominibus Constantinopolitani et Romani, anno Domini millesimo quinquagesimo quarto'

Nicetas: 'Niceta monachus, qui et Pectoratus, ante praesentiam praefati imperatoris ... anathematizavit quoddam scriptum sub suo nomine ... praetitulatum: De azymo, de sabbato et de nuptiis sacerdotum'; the emperor 'jussit ... praefatum incendi scriptum'; next day 'ultro adiit legatos ... Sic ab eis in communionem receptus et effectus est eorum familiaris amicus'. 'the bread of the Mass' renders 'De azymo'
The reply to Nicetas: 'stultior asino frontem leonis et murum adamantinum frangere tentasti ... potius dicendus Epicurus, quam monachus'. Authorship contested: see contested_claims
The patriarch avoided them: 'Michaële praesentiam eorum et colloquium devitante' (Commemoratio); the sentence: 'praesentiam suam et colloquium denegavit'

The sentence's charges: 'sicut Simoniaci donum Dei vendunt ... sicut Pneumatomachi vel Theumachi absciderunt a symbolo Spiritus sancti processionem a Filio'; curse: 'Michaël abusivus patriarcha ... atque cum eo Leo Achridanus episcopus dictus ... et omnes sequaces eorum ... sint anathema Maranatha'. 'Spirit's going forth from the Son' renders 'processionem a Filio'; condition 'nisi forte resipuerint' (Greek 'ἐὰν μὴ πεισθῶσιν', Will l.16036)

The Edict of the synod: 'homines e tenebris erumpentes, nam ex Hesperia originem ducunt' and 'veluti silvester porcus irruerunt' (Greek 'μονιὸς ἄγριος'); the envoys 'ipsi ex se advenerant nullo modo a papa missi' on 'consilis Argyri'; 'litterarum sigilla adulterata esse deprehensa sunt'. Argyrus: 'ad Argyroum catapanum graecum in Italiam' (Will's prolegomena). 'Greek governor' renders 'catapanum graecum'; the letters themselves 'commenti sunt'
claims.witness: WILL (will_acta-et-scripta-de-controversiis-ecclesiae-graecae-et-latinae-saec-xi-grc-lat_1861.txt) l.15269-15283; 15640-15657; prolegomena l.4151 [OCR 'consilis' for 'consiliis', 'Árgyroum']; l.15608-15612

claims.claim: The synod's anathema: 'Judicatum vero est ... vicesimo vero die praesentis mensis Julii ... anathemate feriendum esse rursum idem impium scriptum, et qui illud ediderunt et scripserunt et consensum aliquem, aut consilium, ut illud fieret, praestiterunt'; Will, note 80: 'die XX. mensis Julii Latini a Michaële anathemate subacti sunt'. 'its makers' compresses the list
The envoys' account: Michael wished to bring them to a council 'ut ostensa charta illorum, quam omnino corruperat transferendo, obruerentur ibidem a populo'

Will on the Edict: 'Hoc decretum omnia genera doli, astutiae, calliditatis, superbiae, mendacii manifestissime prodit ... mendacia mendaciis cumulantur'; on the charge that the pope did not send them: 'O impudentiam et dementiam!'

Leo of Ostia, Chronicle of Monte Cassino, quoted by Will: 'Sed quum jam intra hos dies defuncto papa redire disponerent'; Will dates Leo IX's death 'XIII Cal. Maj. 1054'. The brief now gives Will's date for the death (19 April) instead of Leo of Ostia's line
1059: 'Humbertus sanctae ecclesiae Silvae Candidae episcopus subscripsi', under Nicholas II's election decree (Mirbt no. 229, 'Papstwahlgesetz (1059)')
Close, Will on the sentence: 'inde separatio et perfecta et consummata est atque permanet'
Card: Keroularios's two letters to Peter of Antioch: 'binas literas ad Petrum Antiochenum dedit, in quibus quum crimina priora Romanae ecclesiae facta repetit tum alia nova addit'
Card: the paper kept: 'Prototypum vero ... combustum non est, sed in sacro chartophylacis secreto repositum, ad perpetuum eorum dedecus'

Card: Will on the Commemoratio as source and its trust: 'fons plurimarum narrationum de separatione ambarum ecclesiarum ex undecimo saeculo ipso factus ... ut ejus fides ... infringi et debilitari non possit'

Card: the emperor's letter in the Edict; Will: 'Huius epistolae mentionem non facit Humbertus in Commem., quia ei ignota fuisse videtur'; 'Imperatorem vero non sponte sua, sed vulgi seditione, quam patriarcha excitaverat, coactum epistolam hanc ... dedisse verisimillimum est'
Card: year: 'C. undecimo' variant; Will: 'Multi enim legationem ad a. 1053 referunt, sed quum anno demum 1054 legati missi sint'; Leo's letter 'data est mense Januario (a. 1054), indictione VII'
Card: Mirbt's heading '227. 3. Bruch zwischen Rom und Byzanz (13. Juli 1054)'
Card: the palace Pigi: 'intra palatium Pigi'; 'diverterunt ad palatium Pigi'

Card: Wibert gives the reply to Nicetas to Frederick: 'Dominus quoque Fredericus tunc cancellarius ... invective respondit quibusdam objectionibus, quas ediderat Niceta'; Will: Höfler, Giesebrecht 'aliique recentiores secuti'; Will's case for Humbert from 'in superiori nostra narratione, ubi commentis complicum tuorum, Michaelis ... et Leonis Acridani voluimus obviare'
Will dates the sending: 'quos Leo ad pacem restituendam Constantinopolim mittere non neglexit (m. Januario 1054)'; the emperor 'benigne excepit et nonnullos dies in palatio suo retinuit'

Michael's side on the meeting: letter I to Peter of Antioch, 'nulla penitus nos salutatione impertiti nec sustinentes vel minimum capita sua inclinare ... neque etiam omnino admittentes post metropolitanos ... sedere'; letter II, they refused to come before him; Will's note 9: 'prorsus adversatur Humberti narrationi'; Will note 6: 'quomodo factum sit, ut colloquium non institueretur'

The edict on the creed: 'quod sacrosanctum symbolum ... adulterare nolumus nec, ut illi, ex Patre et Filio Spiritum sanctum ... sed ex Patre dicimus procedere'; Will note 18: the question first raised here in these quarrels
Gfrörer held the Dialogue was brought from Rome: 'id quod Gfrörer ... opinatur'; Will argues against

contested_claims.claim: Who wrote the reply to Nicetas
sides: Wibert of Toul, Life of Leo IX II.9 (quoted by Will l.13143-13145), followed by Höfler and Giesebrecht (l.13146-13147): Frederick the chancellor
Cornelius Will (l.13148-13158): Humbert, from the reply's reference back to the Dialogue; Will's series lists it as 'Humberti responsio' (l.1537)
The Edict of Keroularios's synod (l.15640-15657): the envoys came on Argyrus's advice, not sent by the pope, with forged seals
The envoys' Commemoratio (l.14905-14909, 14924-14928): Michael corrupted the translation of their sentence; the emperor found he had falsified it
Cornelius Will (l.15100-15102, 15629): sides with the envoys
The Commemoratio's 'XVII Kal Augusti', read by Will as 16 July (note 80, l.16290-16296; note 4, l.15213-15216)
Mirbt's heading, '13. Juli 1054' (l.9865)

contested_claims.claim: Why the envoys and the patriarch never met
sides: The envoys' account and sentence: Michael avoided them and refused to meet (l.14823-14824, 15031)

Michael's letters to Peter of Antioch: they would not greet him, bow, or sit below his metropolitans, and refused to come before him (l.17206-17225, 18183-18195); Will grants the description shows why no meeting happened (note 6)
Wibert of Toul, quoted by Will: at Constantinople during the legation (l.8345-8348)
Gfrörer, reported by Will: brought from Rome (l.8350-8351)

absent_details.note: The held own-words texts are the Commemoratio and the reply (both attributed), the sentence and the Dialogue, all in Will

claims.claim: Scene, Annals 882: the Northmen 'usque circa Laudunum castellum venerunt ... disponentes Remi venire'; 'Quod pro certo audiens Hincmarus episcopus ... vix noctu cum corpore sancti Remigii et ornamentis Remensis ecclesiae, sicut infirmitas corporis eius poscebat, sella gestatoria deportatus, et canonicis ac monachis atque sanctimonialibus hac illacque dispersis, ultra Matronam in quadam villa quae Sparnacus nominatur vix fuga lapsus pervenit'; 'civitatem, quam nec murus nec humana manus defendit, Dei potentia et sanctorum merita, ne illam ingrederentur, defenderunt'. One clause: no wall or human hand defended the city
The annals end in 882: the 882 entry is the last before Waitz's Emendanda

Authorship from 861: heading 'AUCTORE HINCMARO ARCHIEPISCOPO REMENSI'; Pertz's preface (signed 'G. H PERTZ.', l.249): 'annalium inde ab a. 861. auctorem ipsum Hincmarum fuisse, extra dubium venit'; 'quaedam ab eo allata vix cuiquam praeter Hincmarum nota esse potuerunt'; Pertz: 'archiepiscopi illius, non solum in iure canonico, sed et in rebus ipsis suo tempore gestis versatissimi'; Pertz: 'Hincmarum vero, in rebus praecipue suis, maiore circumspectione consulendum esse'
claims.witness: BERT l.3530; Pertz's preface in BERT l.203-214, 247-249

claims.claim: 849: Gottschalk condemned at Quierzy 'ad Hincmarum tunc Remensem archiepiscopum fuit remissus, ut in custodia detineretur' (Nicolás Antonio)
Prudentius quarrel: Hincmar's 861 notice ('heresis defensor acerrimus'); his letter to Egilo on the 859 entry

The nephew: 'Hincmarus Laudunensis nomine tantum episcopus, homo insolentiae singularis ... contra regem rebellans ... metropolitano suo se inde regulariter commonenti oboedire contempnens'; Douzy, August 871: 'de causis certissimis regulariter accusatus atque convictus, depositionis iudicium regulare suscepit'. Hostile witness (the uncle's annals)

Nephew: Krusch, 'Hincmarus Laudunensis, nepos ipsius'; Mansi 16: 'pro nepote adversus vim externam pugnat avunculus' (Ludovicus Cellotius's preface to the opuscula of 868, 'Porrecta Carolo regi apud Pistas'); 'cum avunculo disceptat nepos'
claims.witness: SRM3 (passiones-vitaeque-sanctorum-merovingici-mgh-srm-3-lat_krusch1896.txt) l.19239; MANSI16 (mansi_sacrorum-conciliorum-collectio-tomus-16-lat_welter-facsimile1902.txt) l.75399-75418, 75454 [OCR long s: 'fe', 'pugnat avunculus']

claims.claim: Mansi's note on Douzy: 'Quo autem pacto ad synodum hanc perductus ... ab episcopali remotus sit officio, tum deinde in exilium missus, ferro vinctus, ac denique oculis caecatus, fuse narrat Hincmarus ipse in libello proclamationis quem Joanni papae postea oblatum'; 'extat tamen Hadriani rescriptum ad synodum, in quo Hincmari depositionem improbat'

Troyes 878: Pope John said 'Hincmarus caecus, si vellet, missam cantaret'; 'fautores Hincmari ... sine praeceptione papae, Hincmarum, vestimentis sacerdotalibus indutum, in praesentiam ipsius papae adduxerunt; indeque sublatum cantantes in ecclesiam illum duxerunt'
Chapters for priests: 'HINCMARI ARCHIEPISCOPI RHEMENSIS ... Ad presbyteros parochiae suae'; his letters 'HINCMARI RHEMENSIS EPISTOLAE ALIQUOT'

Krusch on Hincmar: 'Homo vanus fallaxque idem delicatissimus erat, fabulasque quas sibi excogitavit fallaciis deliciisque condivit. Sermone prolixo usus, periodos formavit, quae spiritum intercludunt neque sine angore legi possunt'
Life of Remigius: 'VITA REMIGII EPISCOPI REMENSIS AUCTORE HINCMARO'
Card: Douzy acts sent 'per Actardum venerabilem episcopum ... ad apostolicam sedem'; the synod at the king's petition
Card: the 849 entry: Bouquet's note (signed 'BOUQ.'), 'ab Hincmaro interpolatum suspicatur'; Pertz: Hincmar's correcting 're ipsa patet'
Ordination 845: 'Concilium Belvacense ... in quo inter cetera ordinatus est Hincmarus'
Death 882: Mommsen, the annals 'finientes anno quo hic obiit 882'

The nephew's complaint to John VIII: 'Reclamatio et proclamatio Hincmari, qui quondam praeerat ecclesiae Laudunensi'; 'violentia hostili in medio itinere segregatus sum ab ovibus meis'; 'transmissus sum in exilium ... ferro vinctus custoditus sum. Duobus annis ferme peractis, insuper caecatus sum'
John VIII to the uncle: 'agnovimus justum fuisse omnino judicium'
Troyes: the supporters acted 'sine praeceptione papae'

The Douzy bishops' letter to Hadrian II, Hincmar named first: the metropolitan 'qui orfanum benigne illum nutrivit, in clericum totondit, litteris erudivit, per singulos gradus ... ad apicem episcopatus provexit'; 'si forte ... apostolicae sedi surreptum fuerit, ut idem ... in gradu restitutus ... quicquid vellet, licenter agere posset, sciens nos de singulis Romam mittere non posse'
claims.witness: MANSI16 l.66365-66390, 66901-66916 [two columns interleaved; long s]

claims.claim: Hincmar's own letter to Hadrian II: the pope's charge that the nephew 'si me tepescente nullam potuit consolationem invenire'; 'Quem utinam non vidissem, minime autem illum me ordinare in episcopum contigisset'
Antonio blames 'laudatus auctor Annalium Bertinianorum', the 'Bertinianus Anonymus, Hincmari metropolitae ... velificatus partibus'
Cellotius's partisanship: 'illustrius aliquid ad Hincmari Rhemensis gloriam'; the nephew brought 'excaecationem sibi carceremque' by 'nova aliqua machinatione in regem'

contested_claims.claim: The conduct of Hincmar of Laon
sides: Hincmar of Reims's annals: insolent, a rebel against the king, deposed by rule at Douzy (BERT l.6939-6977)
The nephew's own complaint to Pope John VIII: seized, exiled, chained and blinded (MANSI17 l.36782-36950); his supporters at Troyes (BERT l.8504-8512)

contested_claims.claim: Whether the deposition at Douzy was just
sides: Pope Hadrian II rejected it, by Mansi's note (MANSI16 l.53133-53137)
Pope John VIII called the judgment just (MANSI16 l.53945-53951)

absent_details.note: No held line gives them. Flodoard's History of the Church of Reims is not held

claims.claim: Scene, De praedestinatione contra Joannem Scotum, preface to Wenilo: 'misisti mihi quamdam schedulam decem et novem capitula continentem ex libro cujusdam Scoti selecta'; 'rogans et monens ut quaecunque in eis a vero exorbitantia comperissem ... responsa'; 'reperi in eis Pelagianae venena perfidiae, et aliquoties Origenis amentiam' ('at times'); 'Intremui, fateor, et expavi tot olim errores cum suis auctoribus jam sopitos nostris denuo temporibus pullulare'. Told in modern words
claims.witness: PL115 (eulogius-cordoba_opera-with-alvarus-vita-eulogii-pl115-lat_migne1852.txt) l.82822, 82839, 82855-82891 [two columns interleaved; OCR 'GuenLont', 'lutremni', 'expavyi', 'denno Llempori- bus']

claims.claim: Hincmar, Annals 861: 'Galindo cognomento Prudentius Trecassinae civitatis episcopus, natione Hispanus; adprime litteris eruditus, qui ante aliquot annos Gotescalco praedestinatiano restiterat, post, felle commotus, contra quosdam episcopos secum heretico resistentes ipsius heresis defensor acerrimus ... moritur'. Hostile witness

The poem: Antonio, 'Imo et ipse Prudentius in carmine quodam ad codicem Evangeliorum praevio Hispania genitum se, ac Celtas deductum, ibique alitum ait'; the verses themselves: 'Hinc ego devoto famulans Prudentius actu ... Hesperia genitus, Celtas deductus et altus'

Authorship of the annals: Hincmar to Egilo, 'domnus Prudentius in annali gestorum nostrorum regum, quae composuit ... Ipsum autem annale quod dico, rex habet'; Pertz (introduction signed 'G. H PERTZ.', l.249): Prudentius died 861 and could not carry the work beyond it; from 861 the author is Hincmar, 'extra dubium'; the first author ended in 835; Waitz: whether official annals 'alii contenderunt, alii in dubium vocaverunt'; Hincmar carried them 'fere usque ad vitae terminum'

Lebeuf's signs, via Pertz's introduction: 'Prudentium ex Hispania oriundum, patrio more ... non epiphaniae sed apparitionis Domini festum dicere'; Roman city names 'Agedincum Senonum ... Tullum Leucorum'; eclipses, comets, aurora, floods, wolves; 'omnia, bona malave, animo pio et benigno divinae omnipotentiae libenter adscribere'; Lebeuf's point is that the part from 861 is 'a prioribus plane diversa'; only the Epiphany usage is 'patrio more'

849: Gottschalk 'publice flagellatus librosque suarum adsertionum igni cremare compulsus est'; Bouquet's note (signed 'BOUQ.'), reprinted by Waitz: 'Doctissimus abbas Lebeuf ... hunc de Gothescalco locum ab Hincmaro interpolatum suspicatur'; Pertz: 'a Prudentio scribi non potuisse viri docti existimant'
Sides: Antonio lists 'Hinc Rabanus Moguntinus, Hincmarus Remensis, Pardulus ... Joannes Scotus ... stetere. Hinc Prudentius noster ... Lupus ... Ratramnus ... Amolo ... Remigius ... Florus'

859: 'Nicolaus pontifex Romanus de gratia Dei et libero arbitrio, de veritate geminae praedestinationis et de sanguine Christi ... fideliter confirmat et catholice decernit'; Hincmar: 'quod per alium non audivimus, nec alibi legimus'
Antonio's answer: 'calumniose et inique dicta contra Prudentium'; 'Nec verum est Prudentium Gotescalcho obstitisse unquam, diversave aut Fidei contraria scripsisse, quod aiunt calumniosi Annales'
Close: 'Trecensemque ipsam ejus quondam ecclesiam, quae in catalogis suorum praesulum sanctum vocat'
Card: councils: 'Parisiensi anno 846; Turonensi IV (alias Parisiensi ...) anno 849; Suessionensi II, 853'
Card: Letter to Hincmar and Pardulus 'scriptum anno 849'; Tractoria: Aeneas 'debere priusquam ordinaretur profiteri, et subscribere quatuor propositionibus'
Card: Hincmar's plea to Egilo: 'necesse est, ut taliter de hoc domno apostolico suggeratis, ne scandalum inde in ecclesia veniat'

Card: manuscript note: 'compositor ejus Prudentius de quibusdam ecclesiasticis dogmatibus non sensit catholice'; Camusat answers, 'Nic. Camusat. Tricassinus, in Promptuario antiquitatum Tricassinae dioecesis'; Camusat: 'ex alicujus fortasse capite'
Card: Galindo: Antonio links the name to 'Galindus Aragoniae comes' and asks 'Quid vero impedit ex eadem progenie cum Galindo nostro Prudentium fuisse?'

Antonio on his teaching: 'Quosdam a Deo fuisse gratuito praedestinatos ad vitam, quosdam imperscrutabili justitia praedestinatos ad poenam'; 'Nicolao I'; Antonio writes after Mauguin's collection of 1650

contested_claims.claim: Whether Prudentius first opposed Gottschalk and then became a defender of heresy
sides: Hincmar, Annals 861 (BERT l.3534-3536): yes; hostile witness
Nicolás Antonio (PL115 l.79391, 79628-79632): a slander; he never opposed Gottschalk
As printed (BERT l.2457-2458)
Lebeuf, in Bouquet's note reprinted by Waitz (l.2495-2505), and Pertz (l.219-226): reworked by Hincmar

absent_details.detail: His birth year, his election as bishop and his family
absent_details.note: No held line gives his birth year or election; Antonio guesses kinship with Count Galindo of Aragon (Inferential-Thin, PL115 l.79275-79276)

claims.claim: Scene, Jonas's preface (Surius, printed by Barralis): 'quamquam me et per triennium Oceani per ora vehit ... Scaldeus molles sulcando vias, madere facit saepe et lenta palus Elnonis plantas, ob venerabilis Amandi Pontificis ferendum suffragium: qui his constitutus in locis veteres Sicambrorum errores Evangelico mucrone coercet'. Told in modern words. He was carried 'per ora' (along the shores)
claims.witness: BARRALIS (barralis_chronologia-sanctorum-insulae-lerinensis-lat_1613.txt) l.36442-36444 [poor OCR: 'Oceani perora', 'Scalteus', 'Elnomis piant as', 'amandi Pottfiat']

claims.claim: Krusch: 'Cum autem constet, Ionam Amando episcopo ad fidem christianam praedicandam adiunctum non solum Scaldim fluvium, sed etiam Scarbeam rivum navigasse eo tempore, quo in Columbani Vita describenda occupatus erat, i. e. ante a. 642'
Munro: 'Jonas ... became a monk at Bobbio, in northern Italy, three years after Columban's death ... obtained material, as he himself said, from the stories told by the saint's companions'

Preface: 'Memini me ante hoc ferme triennium fratrum ... flagitante, vel Beati Bertulfi Abbatis imperio jubente ... fuisse pollicitum, ut almi patris Columbani meo studerem stylo texere gesta'; witnesses alive; 'per venerabiles viros Attalam et Eustasium didicimus'; addressed to Waldebert and Bobolenus
Munro: 'As is usual in such biographies, the miracles are numerous'; 'this biography of Columban is of great value', since 'almost all the accounts of the missionaries from Ireland have been lost'
Krusch dates the Life of Columbanus: 'quem Ionas c. a. 640 Vitae Columbani praemiserat'; 'ante a. 642'
'Theudegisil himself told us of this', in Munro's English

Réomé, 659: 'anno tercio regni domni Clotharii regis ... ex iusso ipsius principes vel genetrices suae praecelse domne Baltilde regine cum ad urbem Cabalonnensem ... Ionas abbas per Riomao sancti Iohannis monasterio preteriens, paucis diebus inibi pro labore itineris quievit, cumque victus precibus fratrum'; Krusch's margin: 659
claims.witness: SRM3 (passiones-vitaeque-sanctorum-merovingici-mgh-srm-3-lat_krusch1896.txt) l.39927-39935 [OCR 'orbem e Caba- lonnensem f']

claims.claim: Krusch on the forgers: 'Aevo enim Carolingico liber Ionae in ipsius sancti monasterio a duobus falsariis retractatus est'; B claims 'se ipsum saeculo VI, ideoque ante Ionam, vixisse'; C, from men 'qui illum saepe vidissent'

Krusch on Vedast: the author 'Ionae peculiare elocutionis genus ita subsecutus sit, ut apud utrumque idem miraculum legatur iisdem fere verbis enarratum'; 'utraque eodem fere tempore ab uno eodemque auctore condita est'; Duchesne 'approbavit'

Close, preface: 'Et si me quempiam laudare repererint qui adhuc superis iunctus sit, non me adulatorem putent ... nec favere cuiquam panegyrico carmine sed digna memoriae commendare'. Told in modern words

claims.claim: Scene, Julian's Elogium: 'vita delectatus est monachorum, contemptisque parentum rerumque mundanarum affectibus, Agaliense monasterium petiit, cujus fugam rabido furore insequens pater, uno tantum maceriae impeditus est obice ... dum percitus in interiora praetenderet, latibulum quo hic vir occulebatur reliquit ... Armata deinde manu Agaliensem cellam impetens gladio, dum quaesitum non invenit, rediens in propriam, ut perditum deploravit'

After: 'Percognita igitur praefatus vir abstinentia parentali, Agaliense illico monasterium adiit, monachumque se in eo multis fere annis decenter exhibuit. Coenobium quoque virginum in Deibiensi villula construxit, ac propriis opibus decoravit. Rector deinde effectus Agaliensis coenobii'

Julian lived in his time and later held the see: Antonio, 'Julianus ... post Quiricum Hildefonsi successorem Toletanus antistes ... qui eum descripsit coaevus'; the Elogium heading 'Ex sancto Juliano in appendice ad librum de Viris illustribus'
'Principali post haec violentia Toletum reducitur, atque inibi post decessoris sui obitum pontifex subrogatur'; 'praesul post secundum Eugenium in sacerdotium consecratur'

'Ascitus autem in pontificatum nono gloriosi Reccesvinthi principis anno, novem annis et duobus fere mensibus clarus habitus fuit ... expletoque octavo decimo praedicti principis anno, sequenti die, decimo Kalendas Februarii, domicilio carnis exuitur, atque in ecclesia beatae Leocadiae tumulatur, ad pedes sui conditus decessoris'

claims.claim: Scene: 'as Beino was travelling near the river Severn, where was a ford, lo, he heard a voice on the other side of the river, inciting dogs to hunt a hare, being that of an Englishman, who spoke as loud as he could, "Cergia"'; 'he immediately returned'; '"My sons, put on your clothes and your shoes, and let us leave this place, for the nation of this man has a strange language, and is abominable ... they have invaded this place, and it will be theirs, and they will keep it in their possession."'

claims.claim: Born to aged parents (summary 'when his parents were in advanced age'); taught by 'a Saint, who was at Caerwent. The name of that saint was Tangusius'

Gwaredauc: 'the king gave to Beino, a place in Arvon, called Gwaredauc'; the woman: 'the land which you possess ... is a township of the father of the child'; '"The child," said Beino, "who is in that woman's arms owns that land, and is heir thereof"'; 'the haughty king returned an arrogant answer'; 'Beino went away and left him under a curse'; Guideuit 'gave to God and Beino for ever, his township, called Kelynauc'

Winefred: the king 'with his sword cut off her head'; restored; 'in the place, where the blood fell to the ground, a fountain arose ... called, after the name of the maiden, WINEFRED'S WELL'; footnote 'A celebrated and copious flowing fountain in Flintshire'

Note: 'He lived in the sixth century, and his life extended to the following, as it is recorded that he founded a religious society, at Clynog Fawr, in Caernarvonshire, in the year 616'; eleven churches named; 'Professor Rees's Welsh Saints, page 268'
